Langevin Monte Carlo with Average Smoothness

The average-smoothness convergence argument and its supporting probability estimates.

Preprint source; checked main sampling proofs

The correspondence uses arXiv:2605.31413v1, identical to the manuscript audited here. Its main average-smoothness LMC, decreasing-step, Laplacian-smooth LMC and fixed-point control-variate SGLD statements are proved for actual Gaussian sampling laws with the source constants. Extended transport endpoints cover arbitrary probability initializations. The Laplacian proof uses exactly C3C^3C3 regularity and the gradient-of-Laplacian condition. The source audit distinguishes this main-theorem scope from broader auxiliary statements not reproduced in full standalone generality; literal full-paper proof coverage is not claimed.

  • Arnak S. Dalalyan and Avetik Karagulyan (2026). Improved Guarantees for Langevin Monte Carlo with Average Smoothness. arXiv preprint arXiv:2605.31413, version 1 (29 May 2026). Full paper

The main sampling theorems and decreasing-step proposition are proved for actual Gaussian laws with the source hypotheses and constants. The source audit records broader auxiliary coverage separately.

The step is X+=X−h∇f(X)+2h ξX^+=X-h\nabla f(X)+\sqrt{2h}\,\xiX+=X−h∇f(X)+2h​ξ, with ξ∼N(0,Ip)\xi\sim\mathcal N(0,I_p)ξ∼N(0,Ip​) independent of XXX. Extra assumptions

Extra A1 — Finite quadratic transport for the signed one-step inequality

Added in this formalization; not an assumption of the paper at the cited location.

The real-valued signed one-step inequality requires W2(ν,π)<∞W_2(\nu,\pi)<\inftyW2​(ν,π)<∞. This makes its signed score-energy formula an inequality of finite real quantities. It is explicit in the displayed theorem and is not explicit in the corresponding paper statement. The displayed constant-step, Laplacian and SGLD global estimates use extended-nonnegative transport and permit every probability initialization, so they do not require Extra A1.

Paper results

Theorem 1

The one-step average-smoothness inequality

Source: Arnak S. Dalalyan and Avetik Karagulyan (2026), Section 2.1, Theorem 1, one-step inequality claim1.

Paper result proved with extra assumptions. The exact printed signed score-energy coefficient is proved for every nonnegative step. The displayed endpoint is real-valued and therefore makes finite initial transport explicit.

Extra assumptions used: Extra A1.

Mathematical statement

Let f:Rp→Rf:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb Rf:Rp→R be differentiable, mmm-strongly convex with M∞M_\inftyM∞​-Lipschitz gradient, where m>0m>0m>0. The coordinate constants are the literal Taylor suprema in the paper, and Mav=p−1∑jMjM_{\rm av}=p^{-1}\sum_j M_jMav​=p−1∑j​Mj​. For the actual independent Gaussian step X+=X−h∇f(X)+2h ZX^+=X-h\nabla f(X)+\sqrt{2h}\,ZX+=X−h∇f(X)+2h​Z, every h≥0h\ge0h≥0 satisfies

W22(ν+,π)≤1−mh1+mhW22(ν,π)+(Mav+m)h2p1+mh+h2(hM∞−1)1+mhEν∥∇f∥2.W_2^2(\nu^+,\pi)\le \frac{1-mh}{1+mh}W_2^2(\nu,\pi)+ \frac{(M_{\rm av}+m)h^2p}{1+mh}+ \frac{h^2(hM_\infty-1)}{1+mh}\mathbb E_\nu\|\nabla f\|^2.W22​(ν+,π)≤1+mh1−mh​W22​(ν,π)+1+mh(Mav​+m)h2p​+1+mhh2(hM∞​−1)​Eν​∥∇f∥2.

The energy comparison, Gaussian smoothing, Brownian orthogonality and transport infimum are proved from these hypotheses. This real-valued local formula is stated for finite quadratic transport, so every signed energy term is defined. The nonnegative global estimates below also cover infinite initial transport.

Theorem 1

Constant-step LMC convergence

Source: Arnak S. Dalalyan and Avetik Karagulyan (2026), Section 2.1, Theorem 1, constant-step inequality claim3.

Paper statement proved. The source coefficient and exponential factor are proved for the actual Gaussian marginal laws and every probability initialization. The displayed bound uses extended-nonnegative transport, so no additional moment assumption is imposed. Its finite real-valued form is a corollary.

Mathematical statement

For every initial probability law ν0\nu_0ν0​ and 0≤h≤1/M∞0\le h\le1/M_\infty0≤h≤1/M∞​, iteration of the actual Gaussian transition satisfies

W22(νk,π)≤e−2mkhW22(ν0,π)+(Mav+m)hp2m.W_2^2(\nu_k,\pi)\le e^{-2mkh}W_2^2(\nu_0,\pi) +\frac{(M_{\rm av}+m)hp}{2m}.W22​(νk​,π)≤e−2mkhW22​(ν0​,π)+2m(Mav​+m)hp​.

The inequality is stated in [0,∞][0,\infty][0,∞], so it includes infinite initial quadratic transport. For finite initial transport, the proof propagates finite moments and derives the recurrence for every actual marginal law. If initial transport is infinite, the nonnegative right-hand side is infinite.

Proposition 1

The decreasing-step schedule

Source: Arnak S. Dalalyan and Avetik Karagulyan (2026), Section 2.3, Proposition 1, prop:VSS; W2VS and kVS.

Paper statement proved. The exact source schedule, burn-in ceiling, error bound and integer accuracy threshold are proved. The source's initial error upper bound supplies the required finiteness; an extended formulation derives it directly.

Mathematical statement

Write κ∞=M∞/m\kappa_\infty=M_\infty/mκ∞​=M∞​/m, κav=Mav/m\kappa_{\rm av}=M_{\rm av}/mκav​=Mav​/m, and suppose W22(ν0,π)≤ε02p/mW_2^2(\nu_0,\pi)\le\varepsilon_0^2p/mW22​(ν0​,π)≤ε02​p/m. Set

k0=⌈κ∞2log⁡+2κ∞ε02κav+1⌉,hk=1M∞+m(k−k0)+.k_0=\left\lceil\frac{\kappa_\infty}{2} \log_+\frac{2\kappa_\infty\varepsilon_0^2}{\kappa_{\rm av}+1}\right\rceil, \qquad h_k=\frac1{M_\infty+m(k-k_0)_+}.k0​=⌈2κ∞​​log+​κav​+12κ∞​ε02​​⌉,hk​=M∞​+m(k−k0​)+​1​.

The actual varying-step chain obeys, for every k≥k0k\ge k_0k≥k0​,

W22(νk,π)≤κav+1κ∞+k−k0pm.W_2^2(\nu_k,\pi)\le \frac{\kappa_{\rm av}+1}{\kappa_\infty+k-k_0}\frac p m.W22​(νk​,π)≤κ∞​+k−k0​κav​+1​mp​.

The literal schedule, positive-part burn-in and iteration ceiling are checked, including zero initial error. The paired statement bounds the real-valued distance, so finiteness of W2(ν0,π)W_2(\nu_0,\pi)W2​(ν0​,π) is a separate hypothesis there; a companion version states the initial bound in [0,∞][0,\infty][0,∞] and derives this finiteness from it.

Theorem 2

LMC under the paper's Laplacian condition

Source: Arnak S. Dalalyan and Avetik Karagulyan (2026), Section 4, Theorem 2 (TeX identifier th:3), inequality claim3c.

Paper statement proved. The exact printed coefficient is proved using the paper's C3C^3C3 and gradient-of-Laplacian hypotheses for every probability initialization. The displayed bound uses extended-nonnegative transport, so no additional moment assumption is imposed. Its finite real-valued form is a corollary.

Mathematical statement

Let f∈C3(Rp)f\in C^3(\mathbb R^p)f∈C3(Rp) be mmm-strongly convex with M∞M_\inftyM∞​-Lipschitz gradient, m>0m>0m>0, and assume exactly

∥∇Δf(x)∥2≤MΔ2p(x∈Rp),MΔ≥0.\|\nabla\Delta f(x)\|^2\le M_\Delta^2p\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^p),\quad M_\Delta\ge0.∥∇Δf(x)∥2≤MΔ2​p(x∈Rp),MΔ​≥0.

For the actual Gaussian LMC chain, every initial probability law ν0\nu_0ν0​ and 0<h<1/M∞0<h<1/M_\infty0<h<1/M∞​,

W2(νk,π)≤(1−mh)kW2(ν0,π)+(2M∞Mav+MΔ)hpm.W_2(\nu_k,\pi)\le(1-mh)^kW_2(\nu_0,\pi) +\frac{(2M_\infty\sqrt{M_{\rm av}}+M_\Delta)h\sqrt p}{m}.W2​(νk​,π)≤(1−mh)kW2​(ν0​,π)+m(2M∞​Mav​​+MΔ​)hp​​.

The proof derives a weighted Dynkin identity for the constructed stationary Brownian diffusion from fresh Gaussian Euler steps. Compact C2C^2C2 approximations of its score preserve precisely the source C3C^3C3 assumption; the Gibbs score moment and gradient-generator bound retain the exact average smoothness. Clipping and the transport infimum give the displayed constant without an optimal-coupling premise. The inequality is stated in [0,∞][0,\infty][0,∞], so it covers every probability initialization, including infinite initial quadratic transport. No Hessian Lipschitz condition or fourth derivative is used.

Theorem 3

Fixed-point control-variate SGLD convergence

Source: Arnak S. Dalalyan and Avetik Karagulyan (2026), Section 5, Theorem 3 (th:sgld), inequality claim-sgld-3a.

Paper statement proved. The source's component RMS seminorm, scaled coordinate-average constant, step restriction and coefficients are unchanged. This source-facing endpoint uses extended-nonnegative transport and permits every probability initialization.

Mathematical statement

Let f=∑i=1nfif=\sum_{i=1}^n f_if=∑i=1n​fi​, each component have a Lipschitz gradient, and the full potential be nmˉn\bar mnmˉ-strongly convex. With its unique minimizer θ∗\theta_*θ∗​, the actual update is

X+=X−hn(∇fI(X)−∇fI(θ∗))+2h Z,X^+=X-hn(\nabla f_I(X)-\nabla f_I(\theta_*))+\sqrt{2h}\,Z,X+=X−hn(∇fI​(X)−∇fI​(θ∗​))+2h​Z,

where the uniform index and standard Gaussian are independent of each other and the initialization. The component seminorms define exactly Mrms2=n−1∑i∥∇fi∥Lip2M_{\rm rms}^2=n^{-1}\sum_i\|\nabla f_i\|_{\rm Lip}^2Mrms2​=n−1∑i​∥∇fi​∥Lip2​, and Mˉav=Mav(f)/n\bar M_{\rm av}=M_{\rm av}(f)/nMˉav​=Mav​(f)/n, as in the source. For 0≤h≤mˉ/(3nMrms2)0\le h\le\bar m/(3nM_{\rm rms}^2)0≤h≤mˉ/(3nMrms2​),

W22(νk,π)≤(1+nmˉh)−kW22(ν0,π)+(Mˉav+2mˉ+2Mrms2mˉ)hpmˉ.W_2^2(\nu_k,\pi)\le(1+n\bar m h)^{-k}W_2^2(\nu_0,\pi) +\left(\bar M_{\rm av}+2\bar m+ \frac{2M_{\rm rms}^2}{\bar m}\right)\frac{hp}{\bar m}.W22​(νk​,π)≤(1+nmˉh)−kW22​(ν0​,π)+(Mˉav​+2mˉ+mˉ2Mrms2​​)mˉhp​.

The estimator is proved unbiased, its variance is computed exactly, and disintegration constructs the required coupling. No convexity assumption on the individual components or additional derivative order is used. The bound is stated in [0,∞][0,\infty][0,∞], so it covers every probability initialization.

What the commands check

Install Git and elan, Lean’s toolchain manager, before cloning. The repository pins the Lean and Mathlib versions; the first cache download requires an internet connection.

lake build AverageLMC checks every proof in the library: when it succeeds, each theorem on this page is proved from the hypotheses displayed in its Lean statement. lake env lean AverageLMC/Check.lean prints the axioms on which the main theorems depend; only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound appear. The local check script also verifies that every displayed Lean excerpt matches the source and that these pages and the PDF regenerate exactly; regenerating them requires Python 3 and Node.js.

The mathematical argument

The argument below gives the estimates in order, including their constants and analytic justification. The adjacent panels identify the corresponding checked Lean statements and explain their role in the proof.

01Gaussian smoothing and the energy comparison §

Objects and hypotheses. Let p≥1p\ge1p≥1, m>0m>0m>0, and let f:Rp→Rf:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb Rf:Rp→R be differentiable, mmm-strongly convex and have an M∞M_\inftyM∞​-Lipschitz gradient. Thus

f(y)≥f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+m2∥y−x∥2,∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤M∞∥x−y∥.f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac m2\|y-x\|^2,\qquad\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|\le M_\infty\|x-y\|.f(y)≥f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+2m​∥y−x∥2,∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤M∞​∥x−y∥.

The Gibbs probability law is π(dx)=Z−1e−f(x)dx\pi(dx)=Z^{-1}e^{-f(x)}dxπ(dx)=Z−1e−f(x)dx, where strong convexity makes 0<Z<∞0<Z<\infty0<Z<∞ and gives finite second moments. A coupling of two probability laws is a joint law with those marginals, and W2W_2W2​ is the infimum of the root-mean-square displacement over couplings. Work first with W2(ν,π)<∞W_2(\nu,\pi)<\inftyW2​(ν,π)<∞. Throughout, a norm of a random vector means ∥X∥L2=(E∥X∥22)1/2\|X\|_{L^2}=(\mathbb E\|X\|_2^2)^{1/2}∥X∥L2​=(E∥X∥22​)1/2; its inner product is E⟨X,Y⟩\mathbb E\langle X,Y\rangleE⟨X,Y⟩. The gradient bound ∥∇f(x)∥≤∥∇f(0)∥+M∞∥x∥\|\nabla f(x)\|\le\|\nabla f(0)\|+M_\infty\|x\|∥∇f(x)∥≤∥∇f(0)∥+M∞​∥x∥ makes all score second moments finite for the states considered. The two Taylor bounds give ∣f(x)∣≤∣f(0)∣+∥∇f(0)∥∥x∥+M∞∥x∥2/2|f(x)|\le|f(0)|+\|\nabla f(0)\|\|x\|+M_\infty\|x\|^2/2∣f(x)∣≤∣f(0)∣+∥∇f(0)∥∥x∥+M∞​∥x∥2/2, justifying the expected potential differences.

The supremum defining MjM_jMj​ gives f(x+aej)≤f(x)+a ∂jf(x)+12Mja2f(x+ae_j)\le f(x)+a\,\partial_jf(x)+\tfrac12M_ja^2f(x+aej​)≤f(x)+a∂j​f(x)+21​Mj​a2 for all xxx and aaa. Insert the coordinates of a standard Gaussian vector ξ\xiξ one at a time, with a=2s ξja=\sqrt{2s}\,\xi_ja=2s​ξj​. Each ξj\xi_jξj​ is centered and independent of the coordinates already inserted, so its linear term has mean zero, while Ea2=2s\mathbb E a^2=2sEa2=2s. Summing over jjj,

Ef(x+2s ξ)−f(x)≤s∑j=1pMj=pMavs(s≥0).\mathbb E f(x+\sqrt{2s}\,\xi)-f(x)\le s\sum_{j=1}^pM_j=pM_{\rm av}s \qquad(s\ge0).Ef(x+2s​ξ)−f(x)≤sj=1∑p​Mj​=pMav​s(s≥0).

Couple ϑ∼ν\vartheta\sim\nuϑ∼ν with Y0∼πY_0\sim\piY0​∼π at finite cost. Let Yt=Y0−∫0t∇f(Ys) ds+BtY_t=Y_0-\int_0^t\nabla f(Y_s)\,ds+B_tYt​=Y0​−∫0t​∇f(Ys​)ds+Bt​, Bt=2WtB_t=\sqrt2W_tBt​=2​Wt​, be the stationary Langevin diffusion driven by a Brownian motion independent of (ϑ,Y0)(\vartheta,Y_0)(ϑ,Y0​). Put A=ϑ−h∇f(ϑ)A=\vartheta-h\nabla f(\vartheta)A=ϑ−h∇f(ϑ), so that A+Bh∼ν+A+B_h\sim\nu^+A+Bh​∼ν+ and Yt∼πY_t\sim\piYt​∼π. Write w=W22(ν+,π)w=W_2^2(\nu^+,\pi)w=W22​(ν+,π) and use L2L^2L2 norms. The common noise cancels:

∥A+Bh−Yh∥2=∥A−Y0∥2+2∫0h⟨A+Bt−Yt,∇f(Yt)⟩ dt.\|A+B_h-Y_h\|^2=\|A-Y_0\|^2+2\int_0^h\langle A+B_t-Y_t,\nabla f(Y_t)\rangle\,dt.∥A+Bh​−Yh​∥2=∥A−Y0​∥2+2∫0h​⟨A+Bt​−Yt​,∇f(Yt​)⟩dt.

Strong convexity bounds the integrand by 2E[f(A+Bt)−f(Yt)]−m∥A+Bt−Yt∥22\mathbb E[f(A+B_t)-f(Y_t)]-m\|A+B_t-Y_t\|^22E[f(A+Bt​)−f(Yt​)]−m∥A+Bt​−Yt​∥2. Stationarity and smoothing at the independent centre AAA give E[f(A+Bt)−f(Yt)]≤E[f(A)−f(Y0)]+pMavt\mathbb E[f(A+B_t)-f(Y_t)]\le\mathbb E[f(A)-f(Y_0)]+pM_{\rm av}tE[f(A+Bt​)−f(Yt​)]≤E[f(A)−f(Y0​)]+pMav​t. The future increment Bh−BtB_h-B_tBh​−Bt​ is orthogonal to A+Bt−YtA+B_t-Y_tA+Bt​−Yt​ and has squared norm 2(h−t)p2(h-t)p2(h−t)p. Since w≤∥A+Bh−Yt∥2w\le\|A+B_h-Y_t\|^2w≤∥A+Bh​−Yt​∥2 for every ttt, this gives ∥A+Bt−Yt∥2≥w−2(h−t)p\|A+B_t-Y_t\|^2\ge w-2(h-t)p∥A+Bt​−Yt​∥2≥w−2(h−t)p. Integrating over [0,h][0,h][0,h] yields

(1+mh) w≤∥A−Y0∥2+2h E[f(A)−f(Y0)]+(Mav+m)h2p.(1+mh)\,w\le\|A-Y_0\|^2+2h\,\mathbb E[f(A)-f(Y_0)]+(M_{\rm av}+m)h^2p.(1+mh)w≤∥A−Y0​∥2+2hE[f(A)−f(Y0​)]+(Mav​+m)h2p.
How the Lean proof follows this argument

integral_stdGaussian_smoothing specializes the independent-coordinate smoothing theorem to the standard Gaussian law. In its finite-coordinate induction, centering removes the linear term and the unit second moment evaluates the quadratic term. gaussian_energy_bound inserts this smoothing inequality into the common-noise stationary comparison; the Brownian orthogonality identity contributes the extra curvature-times-dimension term. All these are integral statements with integrability discharged before linearity is used.

02The one-step Wasserstein bound §

With G=E∥∇f(ϑ)∥2G=\mathbb E\|\nabla f(\vartheta)\|^2G=E∥∇f(ϑ)∥2, strong convexity gives the gradient-step inequality

∥A−Y0∥2≤(1−mh)∥ϑ−Y0∥2+2h E[f(Y0)−f(ϑ)]+h2G,\|A-Y_0\|^2\le(1-mh)\|\vartheta-Y_0\|^2+2h\,\mathbb E[f(Y_0)-f(\vartheta)]+h^2G,∥A−Y0​∥2≤(1−mh)∥ϑ−Y0​∥2+2hE[f(Y0​)−f(ϑ)]+h2G,

and the M∞M_\inftyM∞​-Lipschitz gradient gives the descent inequality 2E[f(A)−f(ϑ)]≤−h(2−hM∞)G2\mathbb E[f(A)-f(\vartheta)]\le-h(2-hM_\infty)G2E[f(A)−f(ϑ)]≤−h(2−hM∞​)G. Adding both to the energy comparison cancels every potential value:

(1+mh) W22(ν+,π)≤(1−mh)∥ϑ−Y0∥2+(Mav+m)h2p+h2(hM∞−1)G.(1+mh)\,W_2^2(\nu^+,\pi)\le(1-mh)\|\vartheta-Y_0\|^2+(M_{\rm av}+m)h^2p +h^2(hM_\infty-1)G.(1+mh)W22​(ν+,π)≤(1−mh)∥ϑ−Y0​∥2+(Mav​+m)h2p+h2(hM∞​−1)G.

The output law does not depend on the initial coupling. Taking the infimum over finite-cost couplings, which is valid also when 1−mh<01-mh<01−mh<0, and dividing by 1+mh1+mh1+mh gives Theorem 1's one-step bound for h>0h>0h>0. At h=0h=0h=0 the transition is the identity.

The cancellation explicitly. Strong convexity at ϑ\varthetaϑ, with comparison point Y0Y_0Y0​, gives

−2hE⟨∇f(ϑ),ϑ−Y0⟩≤2hE[f(Y0)−f(ϑ)]−mh∥ϑ−Y0∥L22.-2h\mathbb E\langle\nabla f(\vartheta),\vartheta-Y_0\rangle\le2h\mathbb E[f(Y_0)-f(\vartheta)]-mh\|\vartheta-Y_0\|_{L^2}^2.−2hE⟨∇f(ϑ),ϑ−Y0​⟩≤2hE[f(Y0​)−f(ϑ)]−mh∥ϑ−Y0​∥L22​.

Expanding ∥ϑ−h∇f(ϑ)−Y0∥L22\|\vartheta-h\nabla f(\vartheta)-Y_0\|_{L^2}^2∥ϑ−h∇f(ϑ)−Y0​∥L22​ produces the gradient-step bound. For the descent bound apply the upper Taylor model at ϑ\varthetaϑ with displacement −h∇f(ϑ)-h\nabla f(\vartheta)−h∇f(ϑ): its linear term is −h∥∇f(ϑ)∥2-h\|\nabla f(\vartheta)\|^2−h∥∇f(ϑ)∥2 and its quadratic term is M∞h2∥∇f(ϑ)∥2/2M_\infty h^2\|\nabla f(\vartheta)\|^2/2M∞​h2∥∇f(ϑ)∥2/2. Adding the two inequalities to the energy comparison cancels f(Y0)f(Y_0)f(Y0​), f(ϑ)f(\vartheta)f(ϑ) and f(A)f(A)f(A) exactly. The remaining score coefficient is h2−2h2+h3M∞=h2(hM∞−1)h^2-2h^2+h^3M_\infty=h^2(hM_\infty-1)h2−2h2+h3M∞​=h2(hM∞​−1). Every denominator is positive because m>0m>0m>0 and h≥0h\ge0h≥0.

How the Lean proof follows this argument

lp_gradient_step and lp_gradient_descent are the two expected deterministic inequalities whose potential terms cancel. lmc_one_step first separates the zero step. In the positive branch, hsm is the exact coordinate smoothing estimate, houtput proves the output transport finite, and wasserstein2_sq_bound_of_finite_couplings passes the common bound to the infimum even when its input-cost coefficient has either sign. The final field normalization divides by the strictly positive denominator.

03Constant-step convergence §

For 0≤h≤1/M∞0\le h\le1/M_\infty0≤h≤1/M∞​ the score term is nonpositive and is dropped. The coordinate bounds give m≤Mav≤M∞m\le M_{\rm av}\le M_\inftym≤Mav​≤M∞​, so t=mh∈[0,1]t=mh\in[0,1]t=mh∈[0,1]. How the Lean proof follows this argument

lmc_one_step_stable first proves that the score correction is nonpositive. lmc_constant_step defines the actual squared-distance sequence as r; lmcLaws_finite allows the one-step theorem to be applied at every index. The block hs is the scalar recurrence after normalization. constant_step_normalized iterates it and uses contraction_le_exp. Finally lmcLaws_const identifies the recursively constructed marginal laws with iteration of the Gaussian transition.

The final enlargement of the nonnegative MΔM_\DeltaMΔ​ term gives precisely the printed coefficient.

How the Lean proof follows this argument

lp_stationary_gradient_pairing_bound bounds the cross term with the actual stationary diffusion and the stated gradient-of-Laplacian assumption. lp_laplacian_one_step_bound combines that pairing with the local integral remainder and gradient-step contraction. laplacian_recurrence_bound_of_global_defect iterates the resulting quadratic-plus-linear scalar estimate. The final theorem lmc_laplacian obtains the required finite-distance recurrence for the actual Gaussian laws and simplifies its constant using the exact Gibbs score moment bound.

06Control-variate SGLD §

Let gI=n(∇fI(ϑ)−∇fI(θ∗))g_I=n(\nabla f_I(\vartheta)-\nabla f_I(\theta_*))gI​=n(∇fI​(ϑ)−∇fI​(θ∗​)). Since ∇f(θ∗)=0\nabla f(\theta_*)=0∇f(θ∗​)=0, its mean over the uniform index is ∇f(ϑ)\nabla f(\vartheta)∇f(ϑ). The SGLD output is the LMC output plus −h(gI−∇f(ϑ))-h(g_I-\nabla f(\vartheta))−h(gI​−∇f(ϑ)), which has conditional mean zero given (ϑ,ξ)(\vartheta,\xi)(ϑ,ξ). Lifting any coupling of the LMC output with π\piπ to the index by disintegration, the cross term vanishes, so

W22(ν+,π)≤W22(νLMC+,π)+h2(E∥gI∥2−E∥∇f(ϑ)∥2).W_2^2(\nu^+,\pi)\le W_2^2(\nu^+_{\rm LMC},\pi) +h^2\bigl(\mathbb E\|g_I\|^2-\mathbb E\|\nabla f(\vartheta)\|^2\bigr).W22​(ν+,π)≤W22​(νLMC+​,π)+h2(E∥gI​∥2−E∥∇f(ϑ)∥2).

Write m=nmˉm=n\bar mm=nmˉ and let MMM be a Lipschitz constant of ∇f\nabla f∇f. The one-step LMC bound turns the score coefficient into h2(hM−1)/(1+mh)−h2≤h2(hM−2)/(1+mh)h^2(hM-1)/(1+mh)-h^2\le h^2(hM-2)/(1+mh)h2(hM−1)/(1+mh)−h2≤h2(hM−2)/(1+mh), which is Proposition 3's first claim. The component seminorms give EI∥gI∥2≤n2Mrms2∥ϑ−θ∗∥2\mathbb E_I\|g_I\|^2\le n^2M_{\rm rms}^2\|\vartheta-\theta_*\|^2EI​∥gI​∥2≤n2Mrms2​∥ϑ−θ∗​∥2, and the Gibbs bound Eπ∥Y−θ∗∥2≤p/m\mathbb E_\pi\|Y-\theta_*\|^2\le p/mEπ​∥Y−θ∗​∥2≤p/m gives E∥ϑ−θ∗∥2≤2W22(ν,π)+2p/m\mathbb E\|\vartheta-\theta_*\|^2\le2W_2^2(\nu,\pi)+2p/mE∥ϑ−θ∗​∥2≤2W22​(ν,π)+2p/m. Take M=R=nMrmsM=R=nM_{\rm rms}M=R=nMrms​. Because m≤Rm\le Rm≤R, the step condition 3R2h≤m3R^2h\le m3R2h≤m implies hR≤1/3hR\le1/3hR≤1/3, so the score term is nonpositive and

rk+1≤(1−mh1+mh+2R2h2)rk+(Mav(f)+m1+mh+2R2m)h2p.r_{k+1}\le\Bigl(\frac{1-mh}{1+mh}+2R^2h^2\Bigr)r_k +\Bigl(\frac{M_{\rm av}(f)+m}{1+mh}+\frac{2R^2}m\Bigr)h^2p.rk+1​≤(1+mh1−mh​+2R2h2)rk​+(1+mhMav​(f)+m​+m2R2​)h2p.

The step condition makes the contraction at most (1+mh)−1(1+mh)^{-1}(1+mh)−1 and the forcing at most (Mav(f)+2m+2R2/m)h2p/(1+mh)(M_{\rm av}(f)+2m+2R^2/m)h^2p/(1+mh)(Mav​(f)+2m+2R2/m)h2p/(1+mh). The fixed point is (Mav(f)+2m+2R2/m)hp/m(M_{\rm av}(f)+2m+2R^2/m)hp/m(Mav​(f)+2m+2R2/m)hp/m. Substituting m=nmˉm=n\bar mm=nmˉ, R=nMrmsR=nM_{\rm rms}R=nMrms​ and Mav(f)=nMˉavM_{\rm av}(f)=n\bar M_{\rm av}Mav​(f)=nMˉav​ gives the SGLD bound; an infinite initial distance makes it trivial.

Why the variance adds. Conditional on (ϑ,ξ)(\vartheta,\xi)(ϑ,ξ), the index III is uniform and its centered error η=gI−∇f(ϑ)\eta=g_I-\nabla f(\vartheta)η=gI​−∇f(ϑ) has mean zero. Expanding a lifted coupled square gives E∥D−hη∥2=E∥D∥2+h2E∥η∥2\mathbb E\|D-h\eta\|^2=\mathbb E\|D\|^2+h^2\mathbb E\|\eta\|^2E∥D−hη∥2=E∥D∥2+h2E∥η∥2, because the conditional expectation of ⟨D,η⟩\langle D,\eta\rangle⟨D,η⟩ is zero. Also EI∥η∥2=EI∥gI∥2−∥∇f(ϑ)∥2\mathbb E_I\|\eta\|^2=\mathbb E_I\|g_I\|^2-\|\nabla f(\vartheta)\|^2EI​∥η∥2=EI​∥gI​∥2−∥∇f(ϑ)∥2. If LiL_iLi​ is the actual Lipschitz seminorm of ∇fi\nabla f_i∇fi​, then

EI∥gI∥2=n∑i∥∇fi(ϑ)−∇fi(θ∗)∥2≤n∑iLi2∥ϑ−θ∗∥2=n2Mrms2∥ϑ−θ∗∥2.\mathbb E_I\|g_I\|^2=n\sum_i\|\nabla f_i(\vartheta)-\nabla f_i(\theta_*)\|^2\le n\sum_iL_i^2\|\vartheta-\theta_*\|^2=n^2M_{\rm rms}^2\|\vartheta-\theta_*\|^2.EI​∥gI​∥2=ni∑​∥∇fi​(ϑ)−∇fi​(θ∗​)∥2≤ni∑​Li2​∥ϑ−θ∗​∥2=n2Mrms2​∥ϑ−θ∗​∥2.

For any coupling with Gibbs, ∥ϑ−θ∗∥2≤2∥ϑ−Y∥2+2∥Y−θ∗∥2\|\vartheta-\theta_*\|^2\le2\|\vartheta-Y\|^2+2\|Y-\theta_*\|^2∥ϑ−θ∗​∥2≤2∥ϑ−Y∥2+2∥Y−θ∗​∥2. Integrate, use the Gibbs second moment, and pass costs to their infimum to obtain the displayed second-moment bound. With R=nMrmsR=nM_{\rm rms}R=nMrms​, the small-step condition 3R2h≤m3R^2h\le m3R2h≤m and m≤Rm\le Rm≤R imply mh≤1/3mh\le1/3mh≤1/3. The forcing comparison uses 2R2h≤m2R^2h\le m2R2h≤m: after multiplication by 1+mh1+mh1+mh, its extra term is at most mhmhmh in the required coefficient. The recurrence fixed point is the forcing divided by 1−(1+mh)−1=mh/(1+mh)1-(1+mh)^{-1}=mh/(1+mh)1−(1+mh)−1=mh/(1+mh). At h=0h=0h=0 the transition is the identity and this division is unnecessary.

How the Lean proof follows this argument

sgld_variance_addition uses a lifted coupling to remove the centered estimator cross term. controlVariateEstimator_second_moment_le bounds the estimator using the actual component Lipschitz seminorms. sgld_one_step_rms combines this variance bound with the one-step LMC comparison. sgld_recurrence_bound uses the small-step condition to bound the contraction and forcing, then sums the affine recurrence. The extended theorem separates infinite initial transport before converting any distance to a real number.
